Test these items: nested select 0..* recursion through contentReference to ViewDefinition.select, child selects use the parent forEach/forEachOrNull context when present, default context is effectively $this when row generators are absent, parent and child columns combine into expected output rows, column name collision and duplicate-name validation behavior, empty nested select and column combinations produce defined output or errors. issues.spec_citation: SQL-on-FHIR v2.1.0-pre ViewDefinition.select.forEachOrNull and Multiple Select Expressions: forEachOrNull produces a row with null values when its collection is empty; parent/child selects repeat parent values for each child item.
issues.evidence: Reproducer: Patient p2 has no contact. View projects id plus select[{forEachOrNull:'contact', select:[{forEach:'telecom', column:[system]}]}]. Actual native registration attempt and forced Python fallback both returned [('p1','email'),('p1','phone')] and dropped p2. Expected includes ('p2', NULL) because the outer forEachOrNull empty record must preserve the subtree's columns as null.
issues.root_cause: No production bug: the synthetic expectation was broader than the SQL-on-FHIR functional model. An enclosing forEachOrNull creates an empty parent row, but a later nested child forEach remains an inner flattening step and can produce no child rows.
issues.resolution: Reverted the first attempted production change after it regressed official foreach.json unionAll cases. Added documentation and a focused integration test for the intended nested forEach-under-forEachOrNull boundary.
